title: Red Bull executive calls Jurgen Klopp departure rumours ‘complete nonsense’
content:
Oliver Mintzlaff, CEO of corporate projects and investments at Red Bull, has described reports that Jurgen Klopp could be close to leaving the organisation as “complete nonsense”.

Klopp has been Red Bull’s global head of soccer since January 2025 but has consistently been linked with a return to coaching.

The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund head coach had most recently been rumoured to be of interest to Real Madrid, following the dismissal of Xabi Alonso in January, and has also regularly been connected with the German national team job, currently occupied by Julian Nagelsmann.

On Thursday, a report published by local Austrian paper Salzburger Nachrichten claimed that Klopp’s position was no longer secure, owing to what it referred to as “a lack of sporting progress” across the clubs in the Red Bull network, despite a contract that runs until 2029.

The story also claimed that Red Bull would not stand in Klopp’s way should he wish to return to coaching, either at club or international level.

Mintzlaff rejected those claims in a statement to The Athletic.

“That’s complete nonsense and totally unfounded,” he said. “On the contrary: We are extremely satisfied with Jurgen Klopp’s work.

“He invests a great deal, is in constant communication with our coaches and sporting directors, and is sustainably developing our Red Bull football philosophy. We are convinced that he is the right man for the job. That’s where we are focusing all our energy and attention.”

The Red Bull network is comprised of Bundesliga club RB Leipzig, Austria’s Red Bull Salzburg, New York Red Bulls in the United States, Red Bull Bragantino in Brazil and RB Omiya Ardija in Japan. Klopp’s role at the company includes developing and scouting coaches.

“I know I can coach a football team, but that doesn’t mean I have to do it until my last day,” he told The Athletic in January, after Alonso’s sacking.

“I wanted to do something different,” he continued. “Red Bull gave me an opportunity to find a role which we have been defining together, step by step. I’m in a place as a person where I’m completely at peace with where I am. I don’t want to be somewhere else.

“It’s been a good time. One year in, five years of experience gained.”

Klopp joined Red Bull after nearly nine years at Liverpool, where he won the Champions League in 2019 and the 2019-20 Premier League title.
